_comment: One disposition and owner for every module in reachability-baseline.json, grouped by coherent subsystem (#33). CONNECT = correct design, no production entry point yet; names the root that would reach it. LIBRARY = published surface or test scaffolding, unreachable by construction and honestly so. RETIRE = superseded; names what replaces it. Checked by scripts/check-reachability-dispositions.py: every baseline module must appear in exactly one group, no group may name a module that is not in the baseline, and every subsystem must be a row in docs/architecture/CONVERGENCE-MATRIX.md. A RETIRE disposition is a decision, not permission to delete -- deletion requires behavioural parity first (#35).

groups.rationale: Privilege middleware and the agent/telemetry protocols are the Conductor's half of ADR-028 and ADR-037; they are written but never installed on the app. Wiring them is #60/#63 work.
Product services with no route or background caller. Each is plausible product surface that was never registered; none owns lifecycle state that the spine must reclaim.
groups.root: main.py route registration or a background loop

groups.rationale: Second-generation persistence helpers that predate the storage decision. ADR-082226-5104 makes PostgreSQL the durable system of record, so these are wiring owed rather than debt.

Three modules. maistro.agents.auditor and maistro.agents.feedback are package __init__.py markers whose siblings hold real code (checks.py; extractor/loop/tracker): they become reachable exactly when those siblings do, and deleting one would break the package below it. maistro.agents.spawner is a genuine re-export shim. Fourteen former members were deleted (#618): nine docstring-only modules with no code, and five package markers standing over nothing at all. The earlier rationale here described all seventeen as 'shims whose only job is to expose an agent implementation', which was wrong for every one of the fourteen -- and its claim that the markers had siblings with real code was false for frank and mason before this change and for forge, scribe and warden_at_arms after it (Codex, #618). tests/test_no_placeholder_modules.py derives the set rather than listing it, and exempts an __init__.py only while its package holds something else.
Agent implementations and supporting stores with no factory or roster entry. #55/#56 make agent invocation a governed Invocation, which is the wiring these need.
The policy-conformance engine of SPEC-206 with no evaluator calling it. ADR-068's approver matrix is the decision it serves and is itself unbuilt (#60).
The ADR-044 AssetInstance replacement, complete but not cut over: routes.py still wires the legacy executor and compositor. ADR-045, which performs the cutover, is still Proposed.
Fakes and a stub provider that exist for tests and for downstream importers building their own harness. Unreachable from a process entry point by construction, and honestly so.
Multi-actor editing sessions with no product surface. ADR-070426-3a1f's A2UI protocol is the consumer, and it is not built.
Docker/Podman runtime selection for the CLI's container commands, with no CLI subcommand reaching it. ADR-093's sandbox isolation model is the consumer.
ADR-063's credential pool and rotation, which #58 moves to Provider selection so rotation reacts to real Invocation outcomes.
groups.root: Provider selection on the Invocation path (#58)

groups.rationale: ADR-047's delivery gateway, complete and uncalled. #57 makes a delivery an auditable Invocation, which is the seam it plugs into.
ADR-086 handlers and recipes with no bus subscription in a shipped process. #61 migrates event families onto one envelope, which is where these get subscribed.
Evolve providers, benchmarks and serialisation with no caller on the cycle path. #51 moves cycles onto canonical Runs, which is when these are reached.
groups.root: maistro_evolve.cycle, once it runs as a canonical Run (#51)

groups.rationale: Home Assistant, CoinSwarm, ntfy and Turing bridges — the homelab product surface, none of it reached from a route or a trigger.
groups.root: a Conductor route or an ADR-086 trigger

groups.rationale: Compaction, scout and steering: graph facilities with no executor calling them. They belong to the traversal half of #44 rather than to lifecycle.

Episodic consolidation and sharing, memory exposure mode, and learnings approval, promotion and skill mutation. ADR-082226-5104 makes these first-class: consolidation is what dreaming executes as a canonical Run. Ranking, retrieval and embeddings left this group at #622, which put the ADR-080 part D score behind the EpisodicStore protocol and wired the ADR-091 assembly that reads it into the agent's prompt builder.
groups.root: the dream consolidation Graph and pgvector retrieval (ADR-082226-5104)

groups.rationale: ADR-036's semantic object layer, Accepted with no consumer. OUT-OF-SCOPE.md already excludes its graph-query language, so the registry is the whole of what must be reached.
groups.root: a subsystem resolving semantic objects through the registry (#34)

groups.rationale: DesignOrchestrateNode registers kind design.orchestrate but sits outside maistro.graph.nodes, so the catalog's eager-import sweep never loads it and the kind is never registered.
groups.root: the maistro.graph.nodes catalog sweep, or an explicit registration at design import

groups.rationale: ADR-052's parallel agent waves. #44 makes fan-out/fan-in graph structure, which is the shape these become rather than a separate wave runtime.
ADR-081/ADR-101 export and import of agents and skills, with no CLI or route calling them. #62 needs backup/restore to preserve canonical Run records, which is the consumer.
Prompt diffing with no caller; the persona eval protocol of ADR-060 is its consumer.
ADR-085 provider-side quota verification and reconciliation. #56 attaches token and cost metadata to the Invocation, which is where these belong.
The autorun loop, harness adapter, rate pacer and apply-agents path. #50 makes RSI cycles canonical Runs over an authorised work source, which is the wiring owed.
groups.root: maistro_rsi.cli / the RSI route, as canonical Runs (#50)

groups.rationale: ADR-038 primitives with no producer: context probing, cross-instance rate coordination and the retry policy. #63 wires reliability signals to real producers.
Classifier decision logging, which ADR-089 wants for measuring classification quality; nothing calls it.
ADR-048 session search with no route. Under ADR-082226-5104 this becomes a pgvector query rather than a separate index.
groups.root: a Conductor session-search route over pgvector (ADR-082226-5104)

groups.rationale: ADR-078's file-based config loader; shipped processes construct settings directly instead.

The #458 interoperability ontology is a published import surface for products to converge onto, not a process entry point: INTEROP_ONTOLOGY_V1 is the executable form of quality/shared-interop-ontology-v1.json and exists to be imported by Builders/Conductor migration issues and the #459 parity suite, none of which may redefine the canonical concepts locally. Its parity and validation behavior is proven by packages/maistro-core/tests/interop/test_contract.py rather than by any runtime path.

ADR-069's signed code registry, ADR-070's repertoire, and the skills catalog, connectors, forge and loader. #59 puts MCP, skill import and signed loading on one governed path, which is where every one of these is reached.

FauxProvider and the harness environment. maistro-core is a published library and this is its test scaffolding for importers; unreachable from a process entry point by construction. The reachability baseline's own comment already records this.

ADR-050/ADR-051 reversibility classification and approval gates. SECURITY.md already states that ReversibilityRegistry is never constructed and Sentinel.resolve_tier never consults it; #57 is the work that makes tool execution a governed Invocation carrying both.
ADR-049's shadow-git rollback and the media tool package, neither reached from a tool registry.
Interchangeable auth backends — JWT, static, cookie, demo cookie and the composite that selects among them. Products wire their own auth instead, so none is selected here.
groups.root: maistro.container auth wiring, or maistro_server middleware

groups.rationale: Guardrails, trust-boundary checks, task policy and Warden flag response: controls that exist but sit off the product path. This is the gap SECURITY.md calls out and #66 closes — construction is not enforcement.
groups.root: the real Conductor chat and tool paths (#66)

groups.rationale: DAG hill-climbing optimises a user's DAG, skills and tools — the artefacts an agent runs with. That is a product capability, and a distinct thing from maistro-rsi, which improves the engine's own codebase under ADR-088. An earlier disposition here called these a duplicate of RSI and retired four of them on that basis; the rationale was wrong and the deletion was reverted. services/optimizer.py and routes/optimizer.py already ship the DAG half of this surface (POST /v1/optimizer/{dag_id}/run, proposals, accept/reject), so these are unfinished extensions of a live feature rather than a second system. hill_climber is its eval-rotation strategy; skill_optimizer extends it to SKILL.md documents and tool schemas; the ui_* trio climbs the product's own UI against canonical examples, with ui_climb_vm naming the microVM as the execution model.
groups.root: services.optimizer / routes.optimizer for the DAG and skill halves; services.hyperlight_executor for the microVM UI loop

groups.rationale: routes/projects.py is a project onboarding flow — intake, scan, deploy, persisted through the Launch DB/Cache/Store — declaring prefix=/v1/projects and never registered in main.py. An earlier disposition called it a duplicate of the canonical project scope surface and marked it RETIRE. That was wrong: maistro.projects owns Workspace/Project *scope*, which is a different thing from an onboarding wizard.

builders/graph_executor.py drives a PipelineGraph to completion on its own traversal loop and writes free-text run.status values ('running', 'completed', 'failed at <node>'), which is a second execution lifecycle over the same work the canonical Run/NodeRun/Attempt records describe. #49 migrates Builders onto canonical Graph/Run; this module is what that migration removes, after parity (#35).

The spec-to-tests-to-code-to-review domain that ADR-090 and ADR-099 keep. builders/dag.py implements SPEC-070226-82ea, which implements ADR-099 — current accepted architecture, not something superseded. builders/orchestrator.py states the convergence rule outright in its own docstring: 'Core owns workflow state. Builders runtime only returns results.' graph.py is the PipelineGraph data model, logger.py records builder actions and XP, runtime.py is the shared runtime for Frank, Mason and Auditor. An earlier disposition marked six of these RETIRE as a 'duplicate lifecycle'; reading them shows only graph_executor.py fits that description.

ADR-044 (Accepted) names store.py, compositor.py and tool.py the legacy LayerRecord path, superseded by the AssetInstance modules, with no data migration and new work on AssetInstance. Verified against the ADR body, not inferred. Retired once ADR-045's cutover lands; ADR-045 is still Proposed and routes.py still wires the legacy executor.

CanvasJobRunner is unstarted, not dead. canvas/executor.py — which is reachable — documents the 'CanvasJobRunner contract' on _execute_claimed; alembic revision 003_canvas_job_lease_203 exists specifically so the runner can take leases and retry; and two dedicated suites cover it, including single-claim-under-contention and lease reaping. An earlier disposition marked it RETIRE because its claim/lease/reap states duplicate the ADR-081626-f383 fence. They do, and #52 is where that is resolved — but a module with a migration, a documented contract from reachable code and concurrency tests is wiring owed, not debt to delete.
groups.root: a canvas worker process started at deploy time; #52 folds it into Attempt execution

groups.rationale: Compatibility re-export. The SSRF guard moved to maistro.security.ssrf in #154; maistro-core is imported by downstream products (AGENTS.md), so the published path stays importable and warns. Nothing in this repository imports it, and nothing should -- an in-repo caller would be a caller of the deprecated path. Unreachable here is the intended state, not pending wiring, and it is removed when the deprecation window closes rather than connected.

The mutation-testing pillar's scripts, unreachable because .github/workflows/mutation.yml is currently a stub. That is a deliberate, documented parking rather than a gap: the workflow's own header states that mutation is disabled until self-hosted runner capacity is restored, that it must not consume GitHub-hosted Actions minutes while parked, and that the implementation, scheduler, checkpointing, history and baselines are kept in the repository precisely so they can be restored. These nine are therefore retained on purpose, and they all become reachable together the moment that workflow runs again. Recorded here because tooling only entered the reachability graph in ADR-082526-aef8 — the decision was always written down, in the workflow file.
groups.root: .github/workflows/mutation.yml, once self-hosted runner capacity is restored and its real job replaces the parked stub

groups.rationale: Operator-invoked CLIs rather than CI gates, and each says so itself. check_assertion_quality reports syntax-level assertion risks and its own docstring defers the real evidence to the mutation ratchet, so wiring it as a blocking gate would assert something it states it cannot certify. generate_repo_tasks (with its _impl) mines retained development history on demand. openrouter_rpm_pacer paces a live account against OpenRouter's shared daily budget, which is an operational act against a real external quota and not something a PR should trigger. Unreachable from CI is the correct state for all four, not a gap to close.

Supporting artifacts for docs/reviews/2026-07-29-rsi-containment-review.md section 9.6, which they are cited by name in. They demonstrate the RLPHD uncertainty band shrinking as an operator rules; they compute nothing the product depends on and assert nothing CI could check. A simulation whose output is a figure in a review document is reachable from that document, which is the only root it needs — running them in CI would spend minutes to reproduce a number already written down.

Reached from a shell script, not from a workflow step or a Python import, which is a blind spot check-reachability.py documents in `_tooling_roots`: "A script invoked through a shell variable, or from a shell script the workflow calls, is not seen -- it errs toward reporting a script unreachable rather than toward silence." This is that case rather than an unwired module. `install.sh` calls it for every write to .env (create, append-once, set-key, ensure-api-keys, check) and `get.sh` calls it to migrate a legacy .env, and `.github/workflows/release-installer.yml` runs `./install.sh --answers-file docs/install/examples/answers-v1-smoke.yaml`, so the code does execute in CI -- one shell frame below what the rooting scan can follow. Its behaviour is covered directly by tests/test_secret_env.py, including four cases that read install.sh and get.sh to assert the call sites still exist, so the wiring cannot rot unnoticed even though the graph cannot see it (#357).
groups.root: install.sh and get.sh, both executed by .github/workflows/release-installer.yml; becomes visible to the graph if tooling rooting ever follows shell invocations

groups.rationale: ac_state_notes remains a per-branch AC-note fold helper loaded by path, so the tooling graph cannot see its runtime edge. ratchet_provenance left this group because the required Vulture Ratchet workflow now executes the full provenance inventory and delegated adapters, which load the shared resolver on every run.

Orphaned by `14a67dd` ("ci: disable autonomous merge safety gate for now"), which deleted `.github/workflows/autonomous-merge.yml` -- the only thing that invoked this script. CONNECT rather than LIBRARY because that commit message says "for now": the gate is meant to run again once #562 decides whether a generated `quality/` ledger counts as trusted surface, at which point it needs a workflow back and this entry pruned. Recorded rather than deleted so the intent survives the pause; a LIBRARY disposition would read as "this was always meant to be import-only", which is the opposite of true -- it is a gate with nothing currently running it.
groups.root: .github/workflows/autonomous-merge.yml, restored once #562 decides whether a generated quality/ ledger is part of the trusted surface and the check can pass for an ordinary change

groups.rationale: Inventories which `quality/**/*.json` state surfaces serialize otherwise-independent PRs (freezing the legacy set rather than migrating any of them) and is exercised only by loading the script itself with importlib.util.spec_from_file_location -- the same shape as ratchet-provenance-helper above: no static import edge exists for this gate to follow, because tests/test_branch_independence.py and tests/test_branch_independence_repository.py load the script by file path rather than importing it by name. Not yet run as a standalone CI step; the contract is enforced today entirely through those two pytest suites.

Reached from a `run:` shell step in the `setup-uv` composite action (`.github/actions/setup-uv/action.yml`), not from a workflow step's `uses:` or a Python import -- the same blind spot `installer-shell-invoked-tooling` above documents: a script invoked through a shell command inside a workflow or composite action is not seen by the import-graph scan, which errs toward reporting a script unreachable rather than toward silence. The code does execute on every job that pulls in `setup-uv`, one shell frame below what the rooting scan can follow. Covered directly by tests/test_build_evidence.py.
groups.root: .github/actions/setup-uv/action.yml's "Record content-addressed setup evidence" step; becomes visible to the graph if tooling rooting ever follows shell invocations inside composite actions
